content: Black exhaust smoke indicates a rich fuel condition. Causes include leaking fuel injectors, failing MAF sensor, clogged air filter, low compression, or a failing ECT sensor. Inspect fuel trim, injectors, and air intake.

White exhaust smoke (especially sweet smell) indicates coolant burning in the combustion chamber. Causes include a blown head gasket, cracked cylinder head, or cracked engine block. Inspect cooling system and perform block test.

Blue exhaust smoke indicates oil burning in the combustion chamber. Causes include worn piston rings, worn valve guides, or leaking valve seals. Inspect PCV system and perform wet/dry compression test.

A sulfur or rotten egg exhaust odor often indicates a failing catalytic converter or contaminated fuel. Inspect catalytic converter efficiency and fuel quality. Check for rich conditions or oil contamination in the exhaust.
